_what: Where the LIVE tool keeps what the update machinery (ops/) reads. When a new version or a new tool goes live, change these paths if they move, and nothing else in ops/ needs to change. See ops/README.md, 'The contract'.
_version_files: Files besides code that make a version what it is. When the last good version has to run (ops/run.sh), every file a person's commit changed since it (and no run wrote) is put back with its code; these are used only if that history cannot be read.
_calendar_rules: 23 September 2026 (collection 358): the H.15 row is posted every business day (h15_daily, 4:15 PM ET), DFEDTARU every day at FRED's measured clock (fred_every_day, 8:01 AM ET; an FOMC decision reaches it the next morning), the Google rows at the end of the UTC day the tool reads (utc_day_end); before, the H.15 week, the FOMC days and 9:00 the next morning. The rules h15_week, fomc and daily_next_morning remain available.
_calendar_read_lag_min: 24 September 2026 (seagate-0924): minutes after the release's time before a row is due, where the tool reads a later post than the release. The state insured rates come from FRED's state release (469), posted the Friday morning after the Department's Thursday 8:30 release (FRED's stamp on 18 September 2026: 8:39 AM ET), so the row is due Friday 8:45 AM ET; the day shown stays Thursday.

conditional_slots.reading_contains: sudden stop: S&P 500 below its high of the prior twenty trading days
conditional_slots.why: the day's Google searches, read the morning they are known, while the S&P 500 is near the sudden stop's market line

_conditional_slots: Runs that are needed only in a given state: while the S&P 500 stands within a quarter of the sudden stop's line (20 percent below its 20-day high), a day's Google searches can complete a call, so each morning's searches are read that morning, weekends included. Otherwise they are read with the day's close.
_fomc_source: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm, read 22 September 2026 (second day of each meeting; the statement at 2:00 PM ET). The Board publishes the next year's calendar each summer: add it here then. The notification says when the list is about to run out.
